findings.evidence: "Default to the lightest channel the recipient reads daily; use email for external or formal records."
findings.fix: Keep the default sentence and cut the channel-role restatement; retain only the non-obvious routing rules (monitored incident path, thread-versus-channel visibility) that the model would not derive.

findings.evidence: "## Route by goal" defines five message types but gives precedence only for the request-plus-escalation mix
findings.fix: Add one precedence rule: "When several goals apply, structure the message by the highest-urgency goal and fold the others into its sections."

findings.evidence: "Do not paste credentials, customer data, or sensitive logs into broad channels. Redact and link to access-controlled evidence."
findings.fix: Keep it but add the less obvious companion trap: pasted links to internal documents also leak titles and access state through link previews; share sanitized titles or access-checked references.

findings.evidence: "Default to the lightest channel the recipient reads daily"
findings.fix: Add the unknown-habits default: "If the recipient's habits are unknown, ask once, or default to the channel where the originating thread lives."

findings.evidence: "Email non-technical stakeholders: critical payment issue delays release one week to March 15; QA retests Thursday, update Friday."
findings.fix: Expand the prompts into full first-person user messages with names, product and channel context, as the trigger queries already do; compressed instructions under-test the audience and unknown-fact handling.

findings.evidence: "## Load by deliverable" lists four reference rows but no load order when one task matches two rows (an email that also needs jargon translation)
findings.fix: Add "Load every matching row: templates first, then translation and channel checks."
